_comment: Synthetic Chrome Trace fixture for test-sycl-gap-causes.py. Hand-built,
never captured from hardware.
The device0/compute queue produces exactly four gaps, one per runtime_idle
cause that parse-sycl-gap-causes.py distinguishes. Every gap is 2,000,000 ns
(2.000 ms), so HOST_OVERLAP_MIN_FRACTION=0.5 demands 1000 us of host-node
coverage to classify as host_overlap. All four must miss that bar for a
different reason, or the cause split is not being observed:
k1->k2  truly_idle             submit window [100,1000) is 900 us wide, so
neither max nor sum can reach 1000 us.
k2->k3  sum_covers_max_does_not submit window [1100,3000) holds three 400 us
k3->k4  submit_pipelined_ahead  k4 submit begins at 3050, before k3's submit
ends at 3100, so the overlap test short-
circuits before any node is considered.
k4->k5  no_submit_span          k5 carries no host_submit_* args and has no
sycl.submit event, so no span resolves.
None of the four may fall to queue_serialization: each gap is far above the
1000 ns epsilon and no event declares depends_on.
The three ggml.op nodes sit at [1200,1600), [1700,2100) and [2200,2600) --
entirely inside the k2->k3 window and outside every other one, so moving or
resizing any of them changes exactly one expected cause.
